1402.name: Stairs On A Humongous Tree

up.description: To the up lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

down.description: To the down lies At A Great Tree.

1402.description:
The stair is a spiral groove worn into the heartwood of a tree so vast
that its trunk seems more a tower than a plant. Lanterns of pale glass
sit in niches along the curve, and the wood glows amber where their
light touches it. The woven silver gate that once closed the foot of the
stair now stands open, and the way down leads back to the roots of the
great tree beside the trade road. Above, the steps climb on into the
green dark.

1403.name: Stairs On A Humongous Tree

up.description: To the up lies Stairs Under A Large Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1403.description:
Here the stair narrows, and the curve of the trunk presses close on one
hand, its bark rubbed smooth by countless soft-soled feet. Slits in the
wood let in thin green light and the hush of leaves, and now and then a
breath of wind carries a sweet, resinous smell. Carved vines twine up
the inner wall, each leaf cut so finely that it seems to tremble. The
steps run down toward the lower flights and up toward a ceiling of pale,
gleaming timber.

1404.name: Stairs Under A Large Platform

up.description: To the up lies Northwest Corner Of The Common Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1404.description:
The stair ends beneath the underside of a great platform, a ceiling of
interwoven boughs grown flat and tight as planking. Light filters down
through the seams in slivers of gold, and the whole structure creaks
softly, like a ship at anchor. A rope-wrapped banister of braided bark
follows the steps, which climb to a square opening where the open air
waits. Below, the flights wind away down the trunk.

1405.name: Stairs On A Humongous Tree

up.description: To the up lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

down.description: To the down lies At A Great Tree.

1405.description:
The lowest flight of the stair ends at a landing high above the roots,
and a ladder of silver rope has been let down from it to the ground.
Where it once hung drawn up, it now dangles free, its rungs swaying
lightly. Great loops of root arch beneath, forming a green-lit hall
between earth and trunk. Cool air rises from below, smelling of leaf-
mould. The steps climb up into the tree, and the ladder leads down.

extra_descs.ladder rope silver rungs:
The ladder is made of braided silver cord, light as a spider's thread
yet strong, with rungs of pale wood. Its upper end is tied off to a ring
in the landing.

1406.name: Stairs On A Humongous Tree

up.description: To the up lies Stairs Under A Large Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1406.description:
A turn of the stair, where the wall of the trunk bulges out into a great
burl, polished by the touch of many hands to the colour of dark honey. A
lantern in a bracket gleams on it. Pale lichens speckle the opposite
wall like scattered coins. A slow tapping echoes somewhere inside the
wood. The steps go up toward the platform and down toward the roots.

1407.name: Stairs Under A Large Platform

up.description: To the up lies Northeast Corner Of The Common Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1407.description:
A short flight of steps runs up to a trapdoor of silver-barked wood set
into the platform's underside. The air here is brighter and moves with
the wind, and the creak of the boughs is louder than lower down. Strands
of ivy trail through gaps in the planks overhead. The stair winds down
around the trunk, its handrail carved with a running pattern of leaves.

1408.name: Stairs On A Humongous Tree

up.description: To the up lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

down.description: To the down lies At A Great Tree.

1408.description:
The lowest flight of the stair curls down to the foot of the tree, where
the door of living bark that once barred it now stands wide, its edges
folded back like petals. Cool air and the scent of earth and roots rise
from the opening. Rings are carved into the wall to mark the tree's old
years, each rimmed with a whisper of silver paint. The steps lead up
into the lantern-lit heights and down to the roots.

1409.name: Stairs On A Humongous Tree

up.description: To the up lies Stairs Under A Large Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1409.description:
The stair coils tightly round the heart of the tree here, its steps
carved from a single spiral ridge of living wood. Knots in the bark have
been polished into little round windows, through which glimpses of
sunlit leaves show. A thin cord of braided vine serves as a handrail.
The smell is of resin and warm sap, and the only sound is the soft creak
of the great tree settling in the wind.

1410.name: Stairs Under A Large Platform

up.description: To the up lies The Southwest Corner Of The Common Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1410.description:
The stair rises into a tight space beneath the platform, its ceiling a
thick weave of branches that creaks and shifts with the breeze. A
lantern of green glass hangs from a hook, tinting the wood and the steps
to the colour of pond water. Each tread has been worn into a shallow
dish by long use. Above, a square opening shows the bright platform, and
below, the flights wind down the trunk.

1411.name: Stairs On A Humongous Tree

up.description: To the up lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

down.description: To the down lies At A Great Tree.

1411.description:
The lowest steps of this stair were once tangled with ivy and wild rose,
but a path has been cut through, and the curtain is now drawn aside.
Thorny stems still cling to the wall, laced with small pink blossoms.
Fallen petals lie thick on the steps, and the smell is sweet and
slightly wild. Light from below shows the cleft in the trunk where the
stair meets the world. The flights climb up into the tree and go down to
the cleft at its foot.

1412.name: Stairs On A Humongous Tree

up.description: To the up lies Stairs Under A Large Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1412.description:
Midway down the trunk the stair broadens into a landing, where an alcove
in the wall holds a bench shaped from a single root. A small window in
the bark looks out over the swaying crowns of lesser trees far below.
Moss grows in a soft green carpet on the steps. The air is cool and full
of the scent of green things. The flights lead up to the platform and
down toward the trunk's foot.

1413.name: Stairs Under A Large Platform

up.description: To the up lies The Southeast Corner Of The Common Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1413.description:
The stair ends beneath a canopy of woven boughs, where bars of light
fall through the cracks in the ceiling in glowing stripes. A handrail of
carved ivy runs beside the steps, worn smooth by many palms. Above, an
opening leads up to the platform, and below, the stair winds down around
the trunk. A cool draught slips up from the depths.

1414.name: The Mages Guild

east.description: To the east lies The North End Of Moredhel Branch.

1414.description:
Shelves spiral up the curve of the walls, crowded with scrolls, glass
spheres and little bound books whose covers shift colour in the light. A
table of grey ash-wood bears a half-finished diagram in silver wire, and
motes of pale light drift lazily near the ceiling. The air tingles
faintly and smells of cedar and lightning. The one way out is the arched
door east, which opens to the end of the branch.

1415.name: The North End Of Moredhel Branch

east.description: To the east lies The Clerics Guild.

south.description: To the south lies On Moredhel Branch.

west.description: To the west lies The Mages Guild.

1415.description:
The branch ends in a small round court, its floor a single great knot of
polished wood. A doorway wreathed in white blossoms leads east to the
Clerics Guild, and a door carved with stars and crescents opens west
into the Mages Guild. Light from a hanging globe pools over the knot,
and the whole court smells of incense and crushed leaves. The branch you
came by runs back south.

1416.name: The Clerics Guild

west.description: To the west lies The North End Of Moredhel Branch.

1416.description:
This chapel was grown rather than built, its walls curving up into a
vaulted ceiling of living wood hung with strands of glowing moss. At its
heart a basin of clear water rests on a pedestal of white stone, ringed
with offerings of blossoms and folded leaves. Low benches of pale birch
face it, and soft songs seem to hang in the air even when the room is
quiet. The only way out is the door west to the end of the branch.

1417.name: The Thieves Guild

east.description: To the east lies On Moredhel Branch.

1417.description:
A low, close room where the lamps are shuttered to a single slit and the
corners are deep with shadow. A table scattered with lock-picks, coils
of fine cord and little velvet pouches sits beneath a hanging net of dry
leaves that rustles at the slightest breath. The floorboards have been
laid to creak in a pattern, and a careful foot learns to step around the
loud ones. The door east is the only way out, onto the branch.

1418.name: On Moredhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies The North End Of Moredhel Branch.

east.description: To the east lies The Warrior's Guild.

south.description: To the south lies The South End Of Moredhel Branch.

west.description: To the west lies The Thieves Guild.

1418.description:
Here the branch widens into a little crossing, with a door cut into the
bark on either hand. The door east is heavy and banded with bronze, its
panels scored by practice blades, while the door west is narrow, dark
and oddly silent on its hinges. The planking is deep green and soft with
moss, and ferns hang from the boughs above. The branch runs on north
toward the clerics and mages, and south back to the platform.

1419.name: The Warrior's Guild

west.description: To the west lies On Moredhel Branch.

1419.description:
A long hall of living wood, its floor sanded smooth for sparring and its
walls hung with targets of woven reed. Racks along the sides hold wooden
practice swords, long bows and quarterstaffs worn pale by use. Beams of
green light fall through high windows, and the boards bear the scuffs of
countless footwork drills. The only door lies west, back onto the
branch.

1420.name: The South End Of Moredhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies On Moredhel Branch.

south.description: To the south lies North Side Of The Common Platform.

1420.description:
Moredhel Branch begins here as a broad living road, its upper surface
flattened and strewn with fine moss. Railings of woven twigs rise on
both sides, and between them the branch runs north into a hush of denser
leaves. Back to the south the common platform is a bright open space,
full of the soft clink of lanterns. Small blue flowers grow in the
crooks where the lesser twigs leave the bough.

1421.name: Northwest Corner Of The Common Platform

east.description: To the east lies North Side Of The Common Platform.

south.description: To the south lies The West Side Of The Common Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs Under A Large Platform.

1421.description:
You step out onto the common platform at its corner, where a rail of
living branches curves around the edge and the ground lies unimaginably
far below. The planks are pale, smooth and warm underfoot, laid so
tightly that no leaf-shadow slips between them. Lanterns hang from the
rail on silver chains, swaying a little in the breeze. The platform
stretches on east along the rail and south along the edge, while the
stairs lead down into the trunk.

1422.name: North Side Of The Common Platform

north.description: To the north lies The South End Of Moredhel Branch.

east.description: To the east lies Northeast Corner Of The Common Platform.

south.description: To the south lies The Middle Of The Common Platform.

west.description: To the west lies Northwest Corner Of The Common Platform.

1422.description:
A broad branch meets the platform's edge here, and the rail breaks to
let it through. The planks are inlaid with a pattern of silver leaves
that catch the lantern light as you walk. Wind-chimes of thin glass
tinkle among the boughs overhead, and the leaves hiss like a distant
sea. The platform spreads out east and west along its edge and south
toward its middle, while the branch called Moredhel climbs away north.

1423.name: Northeast Corner Of The Common Platform

south.description: To the south lies The East Side Of The Common Platform.

west.description: To the west lies North Side Of The Common Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs Under A Large Platform.

1423.description:
The corner of the platform curves to a point here, where the rail swells
into a fat living post carved with a ring of dancing figures. Beyond the
rail the crowns of other great trees stretch away like a green ocean
under the sky. The planks run west along the edge and south along the
rail, and a stair opens in the floor, leading down into the trunk. Gold-
tinted lanterns hang from the post on twisted cords.

extra_descs.post figures dancing ring:
The living post is carved all round with slender dancers, hand in hand,
each wearing a crown of leaves. Their faces are worn faint by the touch
of passing palms.

1424.name: The Elven Magic Shop

south.description: To the south lies The West End Of West Glamredhel Branch.

1424.description:
Glass bottles of every hue fill the shelves, each holding a drifting
mist or a slow, spinning spark. Wands lie in a velvet-lined tray, and a
cloud of tiny lights shifts about the ceiling like a flock of silent
birds. The counter is a slab of polished amber wood engraved with runes
of silver. The air hums faintly and smells of mint and thunder. A door
south opens to the branch.

1425.name: The General Store

south.description: To the south lies West Glamredhel Branch.

1425.description:
Shelves climb to the ceiling, crowded with coils of rope, lanterns,
waterskins, wooden bowls and bundles of arrows tied with ribbon. A
ladder of woven cord leans against one wall, and sacks of dried fruit
slump in a corner. The room smells of tar, wax and cedar, and a brass
bell hangs on a spring over the counter. The door south leads back to
the branch.

1426.name: The Elven Weapon Shop

south.description: To the south lies East Glamredhel Branch.

1426.description:
Bows of yew, ash and horn hang from the curved walls in tidy ranks,
their strings coiled beside them like sleeping snakes. Glass cases hold
daggers with leaf-shaped blades, and on a bench in the corner lies a
half-strung longbow beside a pot of wax. The wooden floor is bare and
swept, and the smell is of oil and cut timber. The door south opens onto
the branch.

1427.name: The Elven Hospital

south.description: To the south lies The East End Of East Glamredhel Branch.

1427.description:
A long bright room where cots of woven willow stand in a line beneath
windows hung with white linen. Bunches of drying herbs sway from the
beams, and on a low table sit jars of salve, rolled bandages and a bowl
of steaming water. The air is clean and sweet with yarrow and mint. The
door south leads out to the balcony at the end of the branch.

1428.name: The West End Of West Glamredhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies The Elven Magic Shop.

east.description: To the east lies West Glamredhel Branch.

south.description: To the south lies The Venison Shop.

1428.description:
The branch ends at a round platform of its own, circled by a rail of
silvery twigs and shaded by a leaning bough thick with glossy leaves. A
door of blue-tinted wood marked with a spiral of stars opens north, and
a plain brown door hung with a carved antler opens south. Small lights
drift in the foliage like fireflies, though no insects hover there. The
way east leads back along the branch.

1429.name: West Glamredhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies The General Store.

east.description: To the east lies The East End Of West Glamredhel Branch.

south.description: To the south lies The Bakery.

west.description: To the west lies The West End Of West Glamredhel Branch.

1429.description:
Two doors face each other across the walkway, one under a sign of a
bundled sheaf and the other beneath a painted loaf. The branch here is
wide and flat, its rail festooned with ivy and strings of dried apples.
Warm bread smells drift out from the south, mixed with the sharper tang
of rope and tar from the north. The branch runs west toward more doors,
and east to the platform.

1430.name: The East End Of West Glamredhel Branch

east.description: To the east lies The West Side Of The Common Platform.

west.description: To the west lies West Glamredhel Branch.

1430.description:
The western branch springs from the platform here, a long arm of pale
wood curving away under a trellis of climbing honeysuckle. Wind-bells of
bone and silver hang along it, and each breath of air sets them
murmuring. The planks are scrubbed and sprinkled with seed-husks, the
leavings of some bird-feeding. Back east the broad platform opens out,
and westward the branch goes on toward the market doors.

1431.name: The West Side Of The Common Platform

north.description: To the north lies Northwest Corner Of The Common Platform.

east.description: To the east lies The Middle Of The Common Platform.

south.description: To the south lies The Southwest Corner Of The Common Platform.

west.description: To the west lies The East End Of West Glamredhel Branch.

1431.description:
Here the platform's planking is stained to a deep honey colour and
rubbed bright by many hands. Clusters of paper lanterns hang from a cord
strung between two posts, and a faint smell of bread drifts in along the
walkway heading west. A shallow carved gutter runs along the rail,
carrying rainwater out to the edge. The platform continues north and
south, while east it opens toward its middle.

1432.name: The Middle Of The Common Platform

north.description: To the north lies North Side Of The Common Platform.

east.description: To the east lies The East Side Of The Common Platform.

south.description: To the south lies The South Side Of The Common Platform.

west.description: To the west lies The West Side Of The Common Platform.

1432.description:
At the heart of the platform the planks are laid in a great spiral of
pale and dark wood, winding in to a small round inlay of silver at the
centre. Overhead the boughs part to frame a disc of sky, and the sun
falls through in a slow bright circle. Benches shaped from single roots
curve around the rim of the spiral. Lantern-lit walkways lead away on
all four sides, north, east, south and west.

extra_descs.inlay silver spiral centre:
The silver inlay is set flush with the planks, a small tree of fine wire
with seven branches. Its roots spread out in the spiral of the floor, as
if the whole platform grew from it.

1433.name: The East Side Of The Common Platform

north.description: To the north lies Northeast Corner Of The Common Platform.

east.description: To the east lies The West End Of East Glamredhel Branch.

south.description: To the south lies The Southeast Corner Of The Common Platform.

west.description: To the west lies The Middle Of The Common Platform.

1433.description:
The platform's rim runs close by here, hung with lanterns shaped like
seed-pods that shine soft gold. A branch leaves the platform east as a
wide walkway, its rail woven into a trellis of climbing white roses. The
planking is worn into pale hollows where many feet have passed, and a
gentle breeze brings the smell of baking and woodsmoke. The platform
carries on north and south along the rail, and west toward its middle.

1434.name: The West End Of East Glamredhel Branch

east.description: To the east lies East Glamredhel Branch.

west.description: To the west lies The East Side Of The Common Platform.

1434.description:
Glamredhel Branch begins its long curve here, springing from the
platform as a boughway broad enough for a wagon. Small lamps hang from
hooks along its rail, and the planks give faintly underfoot, with the
springy feel of a ship's deck. Names of old craftsmen run along the rail
in swirling script. The walkway leads on east toward the shops, and back
west to the open platform.

1435.name: East Glamredhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies The Elven Weapon Shop.

east.description: To the east lies The East End Of East Glamredhel Branch.

south.description: To the south lies The Elven Armor Shop.

west.description: To the west lies The West End Of East Glamredhel Branch.

1435.description:
The branch is busiest here, where doors open on both sides under signs
of carved leaf and steel. The sign over the north door shows a bow
crossed with a blade, and the sign over the south door a mail shirt hung
on a bough. Overhead the boughs lace together into a canopy that
scatters green-gold light across the planks, and bright ribbons tied to
the rail flutter in the wind. West the walkway heads back to the
platform, and east it winds on.

1436.name: The East End Of East Glamredhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies The Elven Hospital.

south.description: To the south lies The Elven Hospitality Inn.

west.description: To the west lies East Glamredhel Branch.

1436.description:
The branch ends in a rounded knob, a broad little balcony whose rail
looks out over a sea of leaves. A door under a carved sprig of healing
herbs opens north, and a wide round door with a hanging lantern opens
south. Pots of lavender and mint stand along the rail, scenting the air.
Back west the walkway returns toward the shops.

1437.name: The Venison Shop

north.description: To the north lies The West End Of West Glamredhel Branch.

1437.description:
Smoked haunches hang from hooks in the rafters, turning slowly in the
warm draught, and strings of dried sausage swing beside them. A heavy
chopping block, scored deep by cleavers, stands at the room's heart, and
jars of salt and juniper line the shelves. The air is thick with
woodsmoke and herbs. A door north opens onto the end of the branch.

1438.name: The Bakery

north.description: To the north lies West Glamredhel Branch.

1438.description:
A great clay oven fills one wall, glowing orange through its iron door
and warming the whole room. Trays of honey cakes, seed loaves and
braided rolls cool on racks of pale wood. The floor is dusted with
flour, and a long table scarred by years of kneading stands in the
middle. The smell is wonderful, sweet with honey and nutty with toasted
grain. The door north returns to the branch.

1439.name: The Elven Armor Shop

north.description: To the north lies East Glamredhel Branch.

1439.description:
Suits of leather and fine scale mail stand on wooden frames shaped like
slender figures, each polished until it gleams. Helms and bracers lie on
shelves, laid out on cloth of green velvet, and a bench holds awls,
rivets and a half-stitched greave. Light from a lantern glints along
rows of buckles on the wall. The door north leads out to the branch.

1440.name: The Elven Hospitality Inn

north.description: To the north lies The East End Of East Glamredhel Branch.

1440.description:
The inn's common room is warm and low, with a hearth of smooth river
stones where a small fire burns and a kettle sings. Chairs of bent wood
sit about tables carved with trailing ivy, and lanterns hang from the
beams in clusters. Rows of keys hang on pegs behind the counter, each
tagged with a painted leaf, and the smell of spiced cider fills the air.
The door north opens onto the end of the branch.

1441.name: The Southwest Corner Of The Common Platform

north.description: To the north lies The West Side Of The Common Platform.

east.description: To the east lies The South Side Of The Common Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs Under A Large Platform.

1441.description:
In this corner a low wall of woven branches curves around a bed of ferns
and moonflowers grown in a trough of earth. The rail beyond is carved
with wading birds, and under the lanterns the planks are scattered with
dew-bright petals. A stairway sunk into the floor spirals down inside
the trunk. The platform runs north along its rail and east along its
edge.

1442.name: The South Side Of The Common Platform

north.description: To the north lies The Middle Of The Common Platform.

east.description: To the east lies The Southeast Corner Of The Common Platform.

south.description: To the south lies The North End Of Eledhel Branch.

west.description: To the west lies The Southwest Corner Of The Common Platform.

1442.description:
The platform narrows here where Eledhel Branch leaves it, a thick bough
of dark, glossy bark that runs away south toward the royal halls. Great
planters of fern and white lilies stand at the mouth of the bough, and
the rail is carved with leaping hounds. The planks are scrubbed so clean
that they seem to hold the light. The platform opens north toward its
middle, and east and west along its edge.

1443.name: The Southeast Corner Of The Common Platform

north.description: To the north lies The East Side Of The Common Platform.

west.description: To the west lies The South Side Of The Common Platform.

down.description: To the down lies Stairs Under A Large Platform.

1443.description:
The platform ends in another corner here, its rail curved to meet itself
around a small carved basin of rainwater. A pair of fruit trees in tubs
of black earth lean over the planks, scattering petals across the pale
wood. A stair in the floor leads down into the great trunk, and the
platform runs north along the rail and west along the edge. Lanterns
shaped like seed-pods hang from the corner posts.

1444.name: The North End Of Eledhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies The South Side Of The Common Platform.

south.description: To the south lies On Eledhel Branch.

1444.description:
Eledhel Branch is the royal road, a thick and glossy bough broad enough
for six to walk abreast. Its planks are laid in a pattern of dark and
pale wood, and its railings are carved with the leaves of the oak, the
beech and the elm. Lanterns of green glass hang at regular intervals,
swaying gently. The platform lies close behind to the north, and the
branch runs on south toward the royal halls.

1445.name: On Eledhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies The North End Of Eledhel Branch.

south.description: To the south lies On Eledhel Branch.

1445.description:
The bough stretches long and straight here, its surface sanded smooth
and sprinkled with the tiny petals of some night-blooming vine. Silken
banners the colour of new leaves hang from the rail, each stitched with
a silver tree. Through the gaps beneath the rail, sunlight dapples the
distant ground far below. The branch runs north toward the platform and
south onward.

1446.name: A Guard Room

east.description: To the east lies On Eledhel Branch.

1446.description:
A watch-room with a view, its single window opening onto the branch and
the green leaf-sea beyond. A table bears a game of carved stones, left
in mid-play, and an hourglass of silver and glass. Spears are racked
beside the door, and a cloak hangs on a peg. The floor is polished by
years of patient waiting. The door east is the way out to the branch.

1447.name: On Eledhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies On Eledhel Branch.

east.description: To the east lies A Guard Room.

south.description: To the south lies On Eledhel Branch.

west.description: To the west lies A Guard Room.

1447.description:
A crossing of the branch, where doors of thick dark wood face each other
beneath lintels carved with crossed spears. Slender lamps burn at each
door, never guttering despite the wind. The planks are scuffed by the
tread of boots, and a polished horn hangs on a hook beside the east
door. Beyond the rail the leaves rustle like a crowd. The branch runs
north and south, with a guard room on either side.

1448.name: A Guard Room

west.description: To the west lies On Eledhel Branch.

1448.description:
A plain, tidy room where spears and long swords stand in racks along the
curved wall. A table of grey wood holds a map of the city's branches
drawn on stretched bark, weighted at its corners with smooth pebbles.
Narrow windows let in the green light and the sound of leaves. Bunks of
woven cord are tucked against the far wall. The door west opens onto the
branch.

1449.name: An Advisor's Office

east.description: To the east lies On Eledhel Branch.

1449.description:
A cosy, book-cluttered office with deep shelves, a small writing desk
and a pair of armchairs facing a window of coloured glass. Rolled maps
lean in a basket, and a lamp throws golden light across a stack of
petitions bound with ribbon. A warm smell of old paper hangs in the air.
A faded tapestry shows the founding of the city. The door east returns
to the branch.

1450.name: On Eledhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies On Eledhel Branch.

east.description: To the east lies An Advisor's Office.

south.description: To the south lies On Eledhel Branch.

west.description: To the west lies An Advisor's Office.

1450.description:
Doors of finely grained pale wood stand on either side of the branch,
each marked by a brass plate inscribed in elegant script. The planks are
brushed clean and polished until they gleam, and a faint sweet smell of
beeswax lingers. Ferns in hanging baskets drip dew from the rail. The
branch leads north toward the platform and south on toward the royal
waiting hall.

1451.name: An Advisor's Office

west.description: To the west lies On Eledhel Branch.

1451.description:
A quiet study lit by a lamp with a shade of green glass. Maps and
scrolls lie across a broad desk of dark burr-wood, and pigeonholes along
one wall are stuffed with sealed letters. The chair is high-backed and
deep, cushioned in grey wool. Everything is orderly, from the quills to
the ink-stones. The door west leads back to the branch.

1452.name: A Guard Room

east.description: To the east lies On Eledhel Branch.

1452.description:
A room of sturdy practicality: a table of scrubbed oak, a rack of
halberds, and a chest bound with a lock of grey iron. A map of the
branches hangs on the wall, pricked with pins of coloured thread. Gentle
light falls from a round window of leaded glass. The boards bear a faint
path along the wall where long patrols have turned. A door east opens
onto the branch.

1453.name: On Eledhel Branch

north.description: To the north lies On Eledhel Branch.

east.description: To the east lies A Guard Room.

south.description: To the south lies The Waiting Area Into The Throne Room.

west.description: To the west lies A Guard Room.

1453.description:
The branch widens before a great carved archway, and the planks are
inlaid with a long band of silver leaves pointing the way. Guard rooms
stand to either side behind sturdy doors, east and west, and the rail is
ornamented with flowing knots of woven brass. The air is cool and still,
with the scent of beeswax and bark. South, the archway opens into the
waiting area of the throne room, and the branch runs back north.

1454.name: A Guard Room

west.description: To the west lies On Eledhel Branch.

1454.description:
A narrow room smelling of oil and leather, where the walls are hung with
quivers, bucklers and scabbards on pegs. A long bench runs beneath the
window, and a rack of whetstones sits beside a lamp. A board scratched
with the names of old watches hangs by the door. The floor shows a path
worn by many pacing boots. The door west returns to the branch.

1455.name: The West Wing Of The Waiting Room

east.description: To the east lies The Waiting Area Into The Throne Room.

1455.description:
A quiet alcove off the waiting hall, cooler than its twin and hung with
curtains of pale silk. A reading desk bears a thick volume of elven
genealogies, and a vase of white lilies scents the air. The window looks
out on the swaying canopy, where the light flickers between the leaves.
A faint sound of lute music drifts in from somewhere. The way out is
east to the main hall.

1456.name: The Waiting Area Into The Throne Room

north.description: To the north lies On Eledhel Branch.

east.description: To the east lies The East Wing Of The Waiting Room.

south.description: To the south lies The Throne Room.

west.description: To the west lies The West Wing Of The Waiting Room.

1456.description:
A grand hall of living wood, its ceiling a vault of woven boughs hung
with glowing globes. Tall benches of white ash face a pair of towering
doors set with silver leaves, and a carpet of deep moss green runs
between them. The walls curve outward into two quiet wings, one reached
east and one west. North the archway returns to the branch outside, and
the great doors south lead to the throne room.

1457.name: The East Wing Of The Waiting Room

west.description: To the west lies The Waiting Area Into The Throne Room.

1457.description:
A small alcove off the waiting hall, with cushioned window-seats
overlooking the shimmering sea of leaves. A low table holds a bowl of
fruit and a pitcher of cool water. Tapestries of green and silver
thread, showing a hunt beneath a pale moon, cover the wall. It is a
place for waiting, and for thinking over what one means to say. The way
back is west into the main waiting area.

1458.name: The Throne Room

north.description: To the north lies The Waiting Area Into The Throne Room.

south.description: To the south lies The Private Stairway.

1458.description:
The throne room is a vast chamber formed by living boughs grown into
pillars and arches, its ceiling lost in a haze of glimmering leaves. At
the far end stands a high seat of silver-grey wood, its back a spray of
carved branches twined with stars. A long carpet of deep green runs
between rows of slender columns, each carved with the history of a
reign. Light of no visible source gilds everything. The doors north lead
back to the waiting hall, and a small door south is closed behind the
throne.

extra_descs.seat throne high:
The seat is grown rather than carved, its arms two boughs that curve
inward and its back a fan of branches studded with tiny silver stars. It
is empty, yet it seems to be waiting.

1459.name: The Private Stairway

north.description: To the north lies The Throne Room.

down.description: To the down lies The Lower Branch.

1459.description:
A narrow stair, hidden behind the throne room, spirals down inside the
heart of the tree. The walls are close and warm, and the steps are
carved with tiny leaf patterns that grip the foot. A single lantern
hangs from a hook, its glow steady and pale. The door north leads back
to the throne room, while the stair continues down toward the lower
branch.

1461.name: The Elvardien Laboratory

north.description: To the north lies The City Street Outside The Adamantium gates.

south.description: To the south lies The Guard's Barracks.

1461.description:
Long benches of dark wood hold alembics, retorts and racks of glass
vials, all joined by a tangle of silver tubing. Bundles of strange roots
and pale mushrooms hang drying from the rafters, and a faint green fume
curls from a bubbling flask. Charts of runes and poisons crowd the
walls, some scorched at the edges. A heavy passage north leads on toward
the adamantium gates of a drow city, while an arch south returns to the
barracks.

1462.name: The Guard's Barracks

north.description: To the north lies The Elvardien Laboratory.

south.description: To the south lies The Lower Branch.

1462.description:
Rows of narrow bunks are built into the curving walls, each with a
folded green blanket and a small shelf for a few treasured things. A
weapon rack stands at the end of every row, and a long table in the
centre is scarred by the marks of dice and blades. The ceiling beams are
blackened with lamp smoke. A narrow door north leads on to the
laboratory, and the arch south opens to the gallery.

1463.name: The Guard's Barracks

east.description: To the east lies The Lower Branch.

1463.description:
Here the barracks are given over to training: grain-filled bags hang
from the beams, and wooden dummies stand scarred by sword strokes. Long
benches line the wall, and above them hang rows of dull practice blades.
A water barrel with a ladle sits in a corner beside a stack of towels.
The low hum of the tree itself fills the room. The arch east opens to
the lower branch.

1464.name: The Lower Branch

north.description: To the north lies The Guard's Barracks.

east.description: To the east lies The Guard's Barracks.

south.description: To the south lies The Lower Branch.

west.description: To the west lies The Guard's Barracks.

1464.description:
A crossroads of galleries cut in the heartwood, where low arches open on
every side. The floor is worn smooth with the tread of countless boots,
and the walls are hung with the old banners of the watch, faded green
and silver. A single iron brazier burns at the junction, its smoke drawn
up into some hidden flue. The archway north leads to barracks, the
arches east and west to more of the same, and the gallery runs back
south.

1465.name: The Guard's Barracks

west.description: To the west lies The Lower Branch.

1465.description:
A smaller barracks chamber, its low ceiling braced with ribs of living
wood. Hammocks of cord hang in two tiers, and each post has hooks for a
cloak, a quiver and a lantern. A small shrine of carved leaves stands in
one corner, with a sprig of fresh greenery laid before it. The air
smells of leather and boiled tea. The only way out is the arch west into
the lower branch.

1466.name: The Lower Branch

north.description: To the north lies The Lower Branch.

south.description: To the south lies The Lower Branch.

up.description: To the up lies The Private Stairway.

1466.description:
The inner corridor opens here into a wider gallery of living wood, its
floor sloping gently with the grain of the tree. Roots as thick as
pillars arch overhead, and lanterns of dim amber hang in the hollows
between them. The air is cool and smells of earth and sap. A stair rises
behind you to the private stairway, and the gallery runs on north and
south.

1467.name: The Lower Branch

north.description: To the north lies The Lower Branch.

east.description: To the east lies The Guard's Barracks.

south.description: To the south lies The Guard's Barracks.

west.description: To the west lies The Guard's Barracks.

1467.description:
Another crossing of the lower gallery, its walls carved with a long
frieze of marching elves beneath streaming banners. A medallion of green
tile, showing a tree in full leaf, is set into the floor to mark the
junction. Arches open east, south and west, and the gallery runs back
north toward the stair. A draught carries the smell of oil and metal.

1468.name: The Guard's Barracks

north.description: To the north lies The Lower Branch.

south.description: To the south lies The Elven Treasury.

1468.description:
A sturdy room near the treasury, with thick roots grown into a rack of
spears along each wall. A heavy table holds a ledger sealed with a brass
clasp and a ring of keys on a hook. The door in the south wall is bound
in silver and kept shut, with a spyhole carved in its centre. The air is
tense and watchful. An opening north leads back to the lower branch.

1469.name: The Elven Treasury

north.description: To the north lies The Guard's Barracks.

1469.description:
A round vault grown inside the tree's heart, its walls lined with
shelves and chests of dark wood bound with silver. Trays of cut gems
glitter beside niches of old crowns resting on cushions of faded velvet.
A runic ward on the lintel flickers faintly. The air is dry and still,
and the only sound is the slow settling of the tree. The door north
leads back to the barracks.

extra_descs.ward rune runic lintel:
The ward is a line of silver runes inlaid in the lintel. They pulse
faintly, in the slow rhythm of a sleeping heart.

1470.name: The Guard's Barracks

east.description: To the east lies The Lower Branch.

1470.description:
This barracks smells of sharpened steel and wax. Racks of long bows and
tall shields stand along the wall, and a worktable bears whetstones,
bowstring wax and a dish of arrowheads. The beams are carved with a
pattern of hawks. A narrow window of bark-thin glass shows nothing but a
deep green dusk. Through the arch east lies the lower branch.

1471.name: The Guard's Barracks

west.description: To the west lies The Lower Branch.

1471.description:
A quiet chamber where off-duty watchers sleep, with rows of cots covered
in grey wool and a rack for boots by the arch. A shuttered lantern hangs
from the central beam, throwing a dim glow across a chest of spare
cloaks. Someone has carved a tally of days into one post. The air is
warm and stale, and smells faintly of pipe-leaf. The arch west leads to
the lower branch.

650400.name: elf citizen elven
650400.long_desc: A slender elf in a cloak of leaf-green strolls along the boughs, humming softly.
650400.description:
She is tall and fine-boned, with swept ears and eyes the colour of new
leaves. Her cloak is clasped with a small silver brooch, and she walks
with the unhurried grace of one who has never feared a fall.

650401.name: elf merchant elven shopkeeper
650401.long_desc: An elven merchant waits behind a counter, arranging wares with careful fingers.
650401.description:
He has a quick, courteous smile and ink-stained fingers. A ring of tiny
keys hangs at his belt, and his eyes miss nothing that passes his door.

650402.name: guard elf elven watchman
650402.long_desc: An elven guard in green and silver stands watch, one hand resting on a slim sword.
650402.description:
The guard wears a shirt of fine linked mail beneath a leaf-green
surcoat. His face is calm and watchful, and he carries himself like one
who has stood many long watches in the high branches.

650403.name: guildmaster master elf elven
650403.long_desc: An elven guildmaster stands here with folded arms, ready to teach those who ask.
650403.description:
Ageless and unhurried, the guildmaster studies each visitor with a long,
measuring look. Years of training others have given the elf a quiet,
patient authority.

650404.name: archmage mage elf elven
650404.long_desc: An elven archmage sits among drifting motes of light, turning a glass sphere in her hands.
650404.description:
Her robes are the grey of morning mist, stitched along the hems with
silver runes that shimmer when she moves. Her eyes are deep and old, and
small sparks gather at her fingertips when she is thinking.

650405.name: warmaster warrior elf elven
650405.long_desc: An elven warmaster paces the sparring floor, watching every stroke with a critical eye.
650405.description:
Lean and scarred, the warmaster moves with the economy of a blade being
drawn. Her hair is bound in a long braid, and a worn sword hangs at her
hip as though it were part of her.

650406.name: captain guard elf elven
650406.long_desc: The captain of the guard stands tall in silver-trimmed mail, surveying her watch.
650406.description:
Captain Elrienna is tall even for an elf, with grey eyes and a long scar
along one cheek. Her silver-trimmed mail is polished bright, and her
leaf-bladed sword never seems far from her hand.

750400.name: cloak elven green leaf
750400.room_desc: A leaf-green elven cloak lies here.
750400.description: Woven of fine grey-green wool, the cloak shifts colour like leaves in the wind. It is light as a sigh and warm as a hearth.

750401.name: brooch silver leaf
750401.room_desc: A silver leaf brooch lies here.
750401.description: A tiny leaf of silver, veined with exquisite lines, made to clasp a cloak. Such work fetches a good price from any collector.

750402.name: mail elven shirt mithril
750402.room_desc: A shirt of fine elven mail lies here.
750402.description: Thousands of tiny rings, each no bigger than a lentil, make up this supple shirt. It weighs almost nothing yet turns a blade like a plate.

750403.name: circlet silver archmage
750403.room_desc: A thin silver circlet lies here.
750403.description: A narrow band of silver, set at the brow with a single pale stone. It hums faintly and sharpens the thoughts of whoever wears it.

750404.name: sword leafblade leaf-bladed captain
750404.room_desc: A long leaf-bladed sword lies here.
750404.description: The blade is broad at the middle and tapers to a needle point, etched with a pattern of veins. Its grip is wound with green silk, and it feels perfectly balanced.
